contents.text: Coordinating conjunctions are used to connect words, phrases, and simple sentences. Some common coordinating conjunctions are and, but, yet, or, and so.

header.text: Use and to connect words, phrases, or sentences that go together or are alike.

contents.text: My sister is going to France and Spain this summer.
I have a pet dog, and my cousin does, too.

header.text: Use but or yet to show a contrast.

contents.text: My brother loves apples but hates apple pie.
Aaron was excited for his performance, yet he still felt nervous.

header.text: Use or to show a choice.

contents.text: Today we can go to the beach or the park.
You can finish your homework now, or you can finish it after school.

header.text: Use so to tell that something happens because of something else.

contents.text: I forgot to set my alarm, so I was late for school.

The weather was cold and rainy, yet hundreds of people still attended the outdoor festival.
